newsitem.title: USA: FBI recovers two priceless Bibles.
newsitem.headline: FBI recovers two priceless Bibles.

text.p: The FBI said on Wednesday it recovered two of four priceless books stolen from the Adams National Historical Site, home of presidents John Adams and John Quincy Adams, his son.

"We think the books are in their original condition, as they were when they were taken," FBI spokesman Peter Ginieres said. The books, both Bibles, were found in a Portsmouth, New Hampshire, health club on Jan. 10 wrapped in towels inside a backpack, according to a published report.

One of those recovered was the "Mendi Bible," a gift from 54 slaves who were members of the African Mendi tribe to John Quincy Adams in the early 1840s after he took their cause to the U.S. Supreme Court and convinced the Southern-dominated bench that the fugitive slaves were entitled to their freedom.
The other was the Bible Concordance, the FBI said.
A team of FBI forensic experts was examining the volumes at the agency's Boston offices, Ginieres said. The books will remain in FBI custody.

Two other valuable volumes remain missing: Block's Ichthyology and a Holy Bible printed in 1772. The National Park Service is offering a $10,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of those responsible for the Nov. 11, 1996, theft at the site in Quincy, Mass.

John Adams, the second president of the United States, was a leader during the American Revolution and signer of the Declaration of Independence who served as an envoy to Great Britain before becoming George Washington's vice president.

His son, John Quincy Adams, became a U.S. senator, served as secretary of state under President James Monroe and became the sixth president. He later returned to Washington as a congressman and attacked measures that would extend slavery.
